newsitem.title: THAILAND: Karen rebels want Burma-Thai gas pipeline halted.
newsitem.headline: Karen rebels want Burma-Thai gas pipeline halted.

text.p: Burmese Karen rebels on Thursday demanded the Burma-Thailand gas pipeline project be halted, charging that an American company is involved and this violates the U.S. economic sanctions against Rangoon.

The pipeline would move gas from a consortium including U.S. firm Unocal, which made it inappropriate for the project to continue, a Karen National Union (KNU) spokesman told Reuters. Unocal is the largest American investor in Burma.
Washington on Tuesday banned new U.S. investment in Burma because of what it said was increased human rights abuses and repression of the democracy movement by Burma's military rulers.

"All in Burma welcome the U.S. sanctions," KNU secretary general Manh Hsa told Reuters. "Since the sanctions have been imposed, we want to...demand that Unocal and PTT halt their gas pipeline project," Manh Hsa said
Although the KNU would not use armed force against the $1.2 billion-project at present, it could not rule out such action later if the group's demand was not met, he added.

"We apologise to all parties concerned for demanding this, but as far as there is no peace and democracy in Burma, no foreign investment should be made in that country," said an aide to hardline KNU leader General Bo Mya.
Work on the 260-km pipeline project owned by state-run Petroleum Authority of Thailand (PTT) began in early April near the northwestern border province of Kanchanaburi.
The pipeline would transport gas from Burma's offshore Yadana gas field to a 2,800-megawatt power station in Thailand's Ratchaburi province. It is due to be completed by mid-1998.
The Yadana project will initially provide 325 million cubic feet of natural gas per day to Thailand. Under the 30-year contract, that will increase to 525 million cubic feet in 1999.

Unocal has a 28.26 percent-interest in the Yadana project. The other partners are the PTT's investment arm, PTT Exploration and Production Plc, Burma's state-run Myanma Oil and Gas Enterprise, and France's Total SA.
The pipeline on the Burmese side runs through areas where KNU guerrillas operate.
PTT officials were not available for comment on the KNU's threat.
KNU and Thai officials said PTT had paid the Thai regional army and border police to provide security against guerrilla attacks during the pipeline's construction.
The KNU, formed in 1948 to fight for greater autonomy from Rangoon for eastern Karen state, is one of a handful of armed rebel groups still fighting Burma's military regime.
